newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rate prospects lift dlr, drag down Ldn stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rate prospects lift dlr, drag down Ldn stocks.

text.p: The possibility of higher interest rates set the pace in financial markets on Monday, lifting the dollar but dragging London stocks down as investors counted the extra cost of doing business.

Most of the day's action was in currency markets where the dollar rose sharply to end up by 1.5 pfennigs and half a yen as the market bet on a rise in interest rates ahead of Tuesday's meeting of U.S. central bank policy-makers.

In equities, London was the only major bourse to open because a public holiday shut down most of Europe and it had a rough day, closing down 48.7 points at 4645.2, after ending at a record high on Friday.

Currency dealers bought dollars ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting. The U.S. currency was also boosted because the mark was pressured by a Bundesbank council member's comments on Germany's efforts to meet the criteria for European monetary union, traders said.
"The dollar's been gaining on short-covering, particularly against the mark, although against the yen there seems to be quite a lot of offers above 116.30," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London.

The dollar, after stumbling because of a sharp jump in Japan's trade surplus, gained over a pfennig and clawed back early yen losses in what dealers described as speculative buying, probably from the other side of the Atlantic. Its effect was exaggerated by the holidays in most of Europe which subdued turnover.

Many dealers focused attention on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Meeting (FOMC) on Tuesday which will consider raising interest rates for the second time in three months in what would be a politically controversial move to stay a step ahead of inflation.
Many European and Wall Street analysts are split down the middle over whether or not the central bank will act to push up short-term rates by another quarter percentage point.

"The market is pretty confused at this point," said Dave Connors, manager of government bond trading at Credit Suisse First Boston. "If you ask most people their opinion, the honest answer is, 'I don't know.'"

Arguing for another rate rise: an economy that has been growing too quickly for its own good, a tight jobs market (the unemployment rate is at its lowest level in over 23 years), rising wages and a stock market that may be too exuberant.
Arguing against: an expected slowdown in the economy, scant sign of any pick-up in inflation, increased worker productivity and spare capacity in the industrial sector.
Some European economists, however , saw the odds for a rate increase improving.

"Many are looking for a 25-basis-point hike (in the federal funds rate) and if this doesn't happen there might be some disappointment...but we're pretty well settled in the 1.70-mark area for now," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.

The dollar had earlier taken fright at data which showed Japan's overall trade surplus ballooned 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen ($7.2 billion). But it later climbed to over 116 yen from its overnight lows of 114. 85 and over 1.71 marks versus 1.6944 in late trade on Friday.

In equities too, investors had the FOMC meeting on their mind and London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index closed sharply down, tracking Wall Street lower as the market fretted that higher rates would hit profit margins.
Retreating from Friday's record close, the FTSE 100 index closed 48.7 points lower at 4,645.2.
Analysts were not surprised at London's bout of nerves after its record-breaking post-election surge. The bourse hit its ninth closing high in the last 11 sessions, at 4,693.9 points, on Friday.

"This is another correction that's been waiting to happen," said Andy Hartwill, strategist at SocGen. "We have seen the best of it for the time being, add in Wall Street coming in weaker and it was always going to be a difficult day."
CLOSING STOCK PRICES
London's FTSE 100 ended down 48.7 points at 4,645.2.
Paris and Frankfurt were closed.
CURRENCIES
The dollar stood at 1.7105 marks and 116.01 yen in late trade compared with 1.6944 marks and 115.53 yen on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $341.25 versus London's close of $344.75 on Friday. Silver was at $4.67, down four cents.
